questions: Q1: What is the current structure and content of SKILL.md, and how far is it from the 10-section progressive-disclosure target?
Q2: What CLI surface tokens (subcommands, flags, enum values) are missing from the existing commands.md?
Q3: Is the install/update documentation still referencing the old npm flow, or has it been updated for the GitHub-release-asset flow (PR #86)?
Q4: How does the skill install mechanism work, and will adding new reference files break it?
Q5: What does the CI sync script need to parse from --help output, and what are the edge cases?
Q6: Are there any existing CI workflows, PR templates, or scripts/ directories that would conflict with the new additions?

answers.answer: SKILL.md has 196 lines with a flat 5-section layout (Guardrails, Environment Setup, Available Commands, Common Workflows, Flag Conventions). The ticket requires 10 sections in a specific order: YAML frontmatter, Workflow, Guardrails, Commands at a glance, Ticket work gotchas, Artifact workflow, Inspection, Writing tickets, Install and update, Source of truth. The frontmatter description is 149 chars (well under the 1024-char limit) and lacks trigger words for ticket-writing, org switching, and broken-install recovery. A complete rewrite is needed, not a patch.

answers.answer: SKILL.md does NOT reference the npm install flow or GitHub release assets at all. It has no install/update section. The update section in commands.md (line 93-98) describes 'hlx update' and auto-update flags correctly but does not explain the underlying mechanism. The recovery.md (which would document the flow) does not exist. The update flow is fully implemented in src/update/**: check.ts fetches from GitHub API for latest release, perform.ts downloads/extracts/validates/swaps, validate.ts checks dist/index.js and --version. The recovery message in src/update/index.ts lines 107-112 points to 'hlx update' and the GitHub releases page.

answers.answer: The skill install mechanism (src/skill/install.ts) copies SKILL.md and then iterates references/ via readdirSync (line 58). Adding new files to references/ (recovery.md, ticket-prompting.md, current-state.md) will be automatically picked up without any code changes. This is confirmed by the install logic at lines 54-60.

answers.answer: The CI sync script must: (1) build via npm ci (which triggers tsc via prepare script), (2) run 'node dist/index.js --help' to get top-level help, (3) parse subcommand names from the usage text, (4) recursively run '--help' on each subcommand (max depth 3: hlx -> library -> comments -> list/post), (5) extract long-form flags (--flag-name) and enum values from usage lines, (6) check each token appears as literal substring in SKILL.md or commands.md (case-sensitive, backticks stripped). The help text format is consistent across all commands (manually written usage() functions with 'Usage:' prefix), making parsing feasible. Edge cases: some subcommands show combined usage for multiple sub-subcommands (e.g., tickets --help lists all tickets subcommands); flags may appear as '--flag <value>' or '--flag' (boolean); enum values appear in angle brackets like '<AUTO|BUILD|FIX|RESEARCH|EXECUTE>'.
evidence: src/index.ts lines 35-63: usage() function shows consistent format with 'hlx <subcmd>' lines
src/tickets/index.ts lines 17-32: ticketsUsage() shows 'hlx tickets <subcmd> [flags]' format
src/tickets/create.ts line 17: help shows '--mode <AUTO|BUILD|FIX|RESEARCH|EXECUTE>' enum syntax
package.json line 19: prepare script runs build (tsc), so npm ci triggers build

statement: This ticket addresses documentation drift and missing CI enforcement in helix-cli's bundled skill. The root cause is a compound gap: (1) SKILL.md was never restructured after the skill was first created, leaving a flat 5-section layout vs. the required 10-section progressive-disclosure format; (2) PR #86 migrated the update mechanism from npm to GitHub release assets but the skill documentation was not updated to reflect this; (3) commands.md has significant flag and subcommand coverage gaps accumulated as the CLI surface grew; (4) no CI mechanism exists to detect skill-docs drift; (5) three reference documents (recovery.md, ticket-prompting.md, current-state.md) specified in the current requirements don't exist yet. All changes are documentation, CI, and scripting — no CLI binary behavior is modified. The skill install mechanism (readdirSync on references/) will automatically pick up new reference files without code changes.
